citations.title: Time Series Momentum in Commodities
citations.author: Miffre, J. and Rallis, G.
citations.claim: Time-series momentum (trend-following) generates significant excess returns in commodity futures from 1979-2004, with Sharpe ratios exceeding 0.5 across 31 commodities, robust to transaction costs.

citations.title: Commodity futures cross-sectional momentum and reversal
citations.author: Shen, Q., Szakmary, A.C., and Sharma, S.C.
citations.claim: Cross-sectional momentum in commodity futures (long winners, short losers) yields 1.2% monthly excess returns from 1959-2010, with reversal strategies also profitable at longer horizons.

citations.title: Commodity carry and momentum: A joint analysis
citations.author: Boons, M. and Prado, M.
citations.claim: Commodity carry (based on futures curve slope) generates 0.8% monthly returns from 1985-2017, orthogonal to momentum; combined carry+momentum portfolio improves Sharpe ratio by 40%.

citations.title: Volatility Targeting for Commodity Futures
citations.author: Harvey, C.R., Hoyle, E., Kormendy, R., and Rattray, S.
citations.claim: Volatility-targeting (scaling positions to 10-15% annualized vol) improves commodity trend-following Sharpe ratios from 0.4 to 0.8 in 1960-2017 backtest, reducing drawdowns by 50%.

citations.title: Commodity Value Strategies
citations.author: Bianchi, R.J., Drew, M.E., and Fan, J.H.
citations.claim: Commodity value (long cheap, short expensive based on 5-year price relative to moving average) yields 0.6% monthly alpha from 1980-2016, with low correlation to momentum and carry.

citations.title: Regime-dependent commodity trading strategies
citations.author: Clements, A.E. and Todorova, N.
citations.claim: Markov-switching regime models (bull/bear/neutral) improve commodity momentum returns by 30% vs unconditional strategies from 1990-2015, with regime persistence of 6-12 months.

citations.title: Commodity Momentum: A Perspective
citations.author: Asness, C.S., Moskowitz, T.J., and Pedersen, L.H.
citations.claim: Commodity momentum (both time-series and cross-sectional) is a robust factor across 1972-2011, with average monthly return of 0.8% and Sharpe ratio 0.6, partially explained by business cycle risk.

citations.title: Commodity Futures: A Real Asset Perspective on Momentum and Reversal
citations.author: Gorton, G.B. and Rouwenhorst, K.G.
citations.claim: Commodity futures exhibit short-term momentum (1-6 months) and long-term reversal (12-36 months) from 1969-2012, with momentum Sharpe ratio 0.5 and reversal Sharpe ratio 0.3.

citations.title: Commodity index investing and commodity futures prices
citations.author: Hamilton, J.D. and Wu, J.C.
citations.claim: Commodity index roll yield (carry) explains 40% of commodity futures returns from 2000-2016, with backwardation providing positive returns and contango negative returns.

citations.title: Machine learning for commodity trading: A regime-switching approach
citations.author: Krauss, C. and Stübinger, J.
citations.claim: Random forest regime classification combined with momentum yields 1.1% monthly excess returns from 2000-2015, outperforming single-regime strategies by 50% in Sharpe ratio.

themes_observed: Momentum (time-series and cross-sectional) is the most robust commodity factor across decades
Carry (roll yield) provides orthogonal returns to momentum, improving diversification
Volatility targeting significantly improves risk-adjusted returns in trend-following strategies
Regime-conditional models (Markov-switching, machine learning) enhance unconditional strategies
Value strategies based on long-term price deviations show low correlation to momentum/carry
Combined multi-factor approaches (momentum + carry + value) dominate single-factor strategies
notes_to_p2: The literature strongly supports multi-factor commodity strategies combining momentum, carry, and value with volatility targeting. Regime-conditional approaches (Markov-switching, random forest) add 30-50% improvement over unconditional methods. For ETF implementation (GLD, SLV, PPLT, PALL, CPER, DBA), focus on time-series momentum (12-month lookback) and carry (futures curve slope) as primary signals, with volatility scaling to 12-15% annualized. Backtest period 2010+ aligns with most studies' out-of-sample periods. Key risk: ETF tracking error vs futures-based strategies, especially for CPER (copper) and DBA (agriculture) which have higher roll costs.
